newsitem.title: LEBANON: More Lebanese arrive from Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: More Lebanese arrive from Sierra Leone.

text.p: A new group of 416 Lebanese nationals who escaped Sierra Leone's coup arrived in Beirut on Saturday from Guinea, a Beirut Airport official said.
This brought the number of Lebanese evacuees who have returned home to 1,824 in three weeks.
"A Middle East Airline jumbo jet arrived from Conakry with 416 Lebanese men, women and children," the official said.
According to the foreign ministry some 2,000 Lebanese lived in the west African country before the coup but Minister of Immigrants Talal Arslan said the total was 9,000.
Another planeload of Lebanese evacuees from Congo Brazzaville is expected to arrive in Beirut later in the evening, the official said.

On Wednesday, a group of 150 Lebanese nationals returned home after escaping political and ethnic fighting in Brazzaville between supporters of President Pascal Lissouba and those of former Marxist military leader Denis Sassou Nguesso.
